purpose: Strict per-URL human quality audit of service, area and guide landing pages
meaning: Editorial judgments, not Google metrics, ranking predictions, conversion measurements or accessibility certification. Weights, anchors, caps and acceptance thresholds are this project's judgments, not requirements prescribed by cited sources.
calculation: Rate each dimension with an integer 0 to 4. weighted = weight * rating / 4. rawScore = sum(weighted). finalScore = round(min(rawScore, all applicable caps)). Retain unrounded component values. Unknown dimensions are null; total is null until all dimensions have evidence. A separately labeled provisional content subtotal is permitted, never normalized to 100.

ratingAnchors.0: Absent, misleading, unusable, or fails the visitor's essential task.
ratingAnchors.1: Major weakness: visitor must infer, reread, search elsewhere or work around the page.
ratingAnchors.2: Usable but materially generic, repetitive, incomplete or inconsistent.
ratingAnchors.3: Strong: concrete task support with only limited, identifiable friction.
ratingAnchors.4: Excellent: fully supported, concise, coherent and demonstrated for this URL; no material unresolved weakness.

dimensions.name: Intent and actionable answer
tests: Title, H1 and first content identify audience, offer or question accurately.
Opening answers what this helps with and the next useful decision.
Service: accepted work, scope and cost route. Area: service availability plus relevant local decision. Guide: usable answer, steps or worked example.
Visitor can take the promised next step without decoding sales language.
dimensions.anchor0: Wrong promise or no usable answer.
dimensions.anchor2: Relevant topic, but the answer or decision arrives late or lacks a key condition.
dimensions.anchor4: Opening and body directly resolve the intended task and its material boundaries.

dimensions.name: Distinct usefulness and local relevance
tests: Explain what this URL adds beyond the nearest sibling and service hub.
For local pages, connect a verified local fact to a concrete website decision; place-name substitution and irrelevant trivia earn no credit.
Public examples are clearly distinguished from clients, work delivered and local premises.
Shared offers and navigation are acceptable; repeated editorial substance must earn its space.
dimensions.anchor0: Interchangeable funnel page with no independent visitor value.
dimensions.anchor2: Some grounded detail, but generic recommendations dominate or the local-to-service connection is weak.
dimensions.anchor4: A visitor gains a specific useful decision, example or resource unavailable from the nearest sibling; locality matters where claimed.

dimensions.name: Evidence, accuracy and scope honesty
tests: Material facts have approved business evidence or relevant dated primary sources.
Inference, proposal, fictional exercise and delivered result remain distinct.
Price, allowance, ownership, update model and exclusions remain consistent.
No invented expertise, relationship, results, location or search guarantee.
dimensions.anchor2: Generally plausible but important claims or assumptions lack clear support.
dimensions.anchor4: Claims are traceable and proportionate; limitations sit beside the affected promise.

dimensions.name: Prose and heading coherence
tests: Each paragraph develops one useful idea with natural complete sentences.
H2 sections advance the argument; H3 sections belong under their H2.
Heading-only reading gives a meaningful outline; no mechanical field labels masquerade as customer-facing prose.
Remove semantic repetition across summary, table, cards, FAQ and closing copy; a summary may recap but must not reproduce the full explanation.
dimensions.anchor0: Incoherent, contradictory or mechanically assembled text.
dimensions.anchor2: Understandable, but repeated ideas or weak transitions create avoidable work.
dimensions.anchor4: Clear progression, informative headings and economical natural prose.

dimensions.name: Glanceable hierarchy and reading burden
tests: A short opening summary exposes the answer or decision without opening disclosures.
Use lists, comparison tables or short steps only where they reduce effort.
Keep critical conditions visible; disclosures hold genuinely optional depth.
Paragraph size, headings, emphasis and section spacing help a phone reader locate a relevant fact.
dimensions.anchor0: Essential answer buried or impossible to locate.
dimensions.anchor2: Some hierarchy, but excessive density, repeated blocks or over-fragmentation slows scanning.
dimensions.anchor4: A quick scan identifies fit, key conditions and next action; deeper reading remains coherent.

dimensions.name: Visual explanation, spacing and color
tests: Inspect actual narrow and wide layouts; no overlap, clipped text, excessive dead space or visually equal competing priorities.
Color and whitespace consistently group related information.
Use a diagram, annotated example or comparison when it explains faster than prose; no mandatory illustration quota.
Text-only execution can earn full credit when it is the clearest solution. Decorative imagery earns no evidence or uniqueness credit.
dimensions.anchor0: Presentation hides meaning or misrepresents evidence.
dimensions.anchor2: Readable but visually noisy, monotonous or needlessly spacious; a complex decision lacks useful explanation.
dimensions.anchor4: Clear hierarchy and balanced spacing; every visual has an explanatory or navigational purpose.

dimensions.name: Accessible comprehension and operation
tests: Check semantic headings, meaningful links, image alternatives and form labels.
Verify keyboard operation, visible unobscured focus, disclosures and error recovery where present.
Test contrast, zoom/reflow, text-spacing overrides, target size and reduced-motion behavior where applicable.
Record automated results plus manual scope and exceptions; passing automation alone is not conformance.
dimensions.anchor2: Core content usable but meaningful barriers remain.
dimensions.anchor4: Relevant manual and automated checks pass with no unresolved material barrier in tested states.

dimensions.name: Useful next step and navigation
tests: Primary action matches the task and explains what happens next.
Related links are specific, selective and useful; no place-name link carpet.
A guide helps before selling; a local page offers standalone value before asking for contact.
Controls and downloads work, and demonstrations are labeled accurately.
dimensions.anchor2: Action works but is vague, poorly placed or surrounded by competing links.
dimensions.anchor4: One clear next action with relevant alternatives and a truthful expectation.

caps.trigger: Verified material false claim, invented client/result/local office, or deceptive functionality.
Primary visitor task blocked by broken action, obstruction or serious accessibility failure.
Main content adds no meaningful task value beyond a sibling/hub; local wording is effectively a place-name substitution or unsupported generic funnel.
Local fact exists but does not materially support the offered service decision; distinctive trivia substitutes for usefulness.
Repeated malformed, contradictory or unfinished prose materially obscures the answer.
Same substantive recommendation repeated in at least three body sections without new decision value, or essential scope hidden behind optional disclosure.
Important factual or commercial claim is neither verified nor clearly bounded as a proposal.

bands.label: Serious failure or insufficient standalone value

acceptance: Target at least 80, no applicable hard cap, every dimension at least 2, and no unresolved material defect. This is an editorial acceptance gate, not permission to change indexing or a release gate replacement.
evidenceRules: Inventory every public URL from the current build; classify redirects, noindex and non-landing routes explicitly. Do not silently reuse historic route counts.
Per-URL text review requires its complete main text, including disclosures, headings, claims and links. A template sample is not individual editorial review.

Rendered layout evidence may be inherited only for unchanged shared components with the same styles and documented coverage. URL-specific overflow, length and disclosure content still need checks. Mark inherited evidence explicitly.
Uninspected visual, interaction or source facts remain unknown, not passed. Do not convert null prior scores into new numeric evidence.
Record exact passages or selectors supporting deductions; regex counts, reading grade, word count and duplicate similarity are triage signals, not quality verdicts.
Use site-level and family-level duplication analysis alongside per-page review. Do not assert a Google spam violation from page count or templates alone.

Preserve factual distinctions, commercial terms, route and indexing policy unless separately authorized. Recommend consolidation or indexing review where warranted; cosmetic edits cannot cure absent purpose.

sources.title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
sources.guidance: Assess originality, completeness, usefulness, evidence and reader satisfaction; descriptive headings and careful production matter.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search
sources.guidance: Doorway abuse includes similar region-targeted intermediaries that funnel visitors. Scaled content abuse concerns pages produced chiefly to manipulate rankings without useful value, regardless of production method. Scale alone does not establish a violation.

sources.title: AI features and your website
sources.guidance: Existing SEO foundations apply; no special AI markup or file is required. Supporting links require indexing and snippet eligibility. Important content should be text-accessible and structured data should match visible content. Eligibility does not guarantee selection.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
sources.guidance: Relevant checks include semantics, text alternatives, keyboard access, visible unobscured focus, labels, contrast, reflow, text spacing and target size. Text contrast generally requires 4.5:1, large text 3:1. Reflow testing uses 320 CSS pixels subject to exceptions. Minimum targets are 24 by 24 CSS pixels or satisfy specified exceptions.

sources.title: How People Read Online: New and Old Findings
sources.guidance: NN/g's own eyetracking research reports persistent scanning behavior across studies. Use clear hierarchy and readily located information; these findings do not establish a universal ideal word count or guarantee conversion gains.

calibration.scope: Built HTML main content and heading inspection only for three representative URLs; not new screenshot, interaction or source-accuracy verification and not a full per-URL audit.
calibration.priorReport: Old report contains 15 page summaries and 2436 ranking entries. Local entries inspected have null scores and template-priority/per-page-check labels. Its 0–10 editorial judgments are not computed component scores and must not be silently rescaled.
observations: Web-design service includes a concrete notes-to-copy example, package boundaries and explicit source-code update model; retain this useful specificity while reviewing overall reading burden.
AI-search guide leads with an answer and includes a worksheet and an explicit fictional example; current platform-specific claims still need independent source validation.

Monona County offers a sourced cabin-stay decision and labels public research honestly, but the same minimum-stay and packing-list advice recurs in summary, table, deliverable details and questions. Evaluate visible and expanded states separately; collapsing repetition is not the same as removing it.
